Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
скала́
Wikipedia bg
седиментна скалà (etymology 1, noun sense 1)
музикална скàла (etymology 2, noun sense 1)

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Proto-Slavic *skala. Cognate with Russian скала́ (skalá), Slovak skala, Slovene skala. Also akin to Ancient Greek σκάλλω (skállō, “stir up, hoe”), Armenian ցելում (cʻelum, “to rend, split”), Old Norse skilja (“to part, separate”). Cf. English shale.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [skɐˈɫa]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian, l-vocalization):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɫa
  • Syllabification(key): ска‧ла

Noun

[edit]

скала́ • (skalá) f (relational adjective ска́лен, diminutive скали́чка)

  2. rock, crag
    Synonyms: канара́ (kanará), зъ́бер (zǎ́ber)
Declension
[edit]

Related terms
[edit]
  • скалист (skalist)

Wikipedia bg

  • Rhymes: -aɫɐ
  • Syllabification(key): ска‧ла

Noun

[edit]

ска́ла • (skála) f

  2. scale (music), range, gamut

Macedonian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈskaɫa]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin scala. Cognate with Greek σκάλα (skála), Albanian shkallë, Aromanian scarã, Italian scala, English scale.

Noun

[edit]

скала • (skala) f (diminutive скаличка)

  1. ladder
  2. stair (a single stair on a staircase)
  3. (in the plural) stairs, staircase
  4. scale (music)
Declension
[edit]
Declension of скала
singular plural
indefinite скала (skala) скали (skali)
definite unspecified скалата (skalata) скалите (skalite)
definite proximal скалава (skalava) скаливе (skalive)
definite distal скалана (skalana) скалине (skaline)
vocative скало (skalo) скали (skali)

Etymology 2

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *skala.

Noun

[edit]

скала • (skala) f

  1. (dialectal) rock
    Synonym: карпа (karpa)
Declension
[edit]
